title: [Maps] Improve error message when WebGL is not available
prompt:
[Maps] Show a friendly message when WebGL is not available

When the browser cannot create a WebGL context, creating or opening any map shows a long, hard to decipher error under the title "Unable to initialize map". The body is a raw dump of the requested context attributes, GPU vendor and renderer strings and the "webglcontextcreationerror" type. Users cannot tell what is wrong or what to do.

Expected: Maps shows a user-friendly, actionable message when the map cannot start because WebGL is unavailable. Other initialization errors keep working as today.

Start in x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/maps/public/connected_components/map_container/map_container.tsx. Keep the change scoped to this feature.
acceptance: When map initialization fails because WebGL is unavailable, the user sees a short plain-language explanation instead of the raw error dump.
The message tells the user what to do (for example enable hardware acceleration or use a browser/device with WebGL support).
Other initialization errors still show their own error text.
The raw technical details are not shown as the main message.
whySuitable: Error state UI in a single container component; spare because the exact wording and WebGL detection approach are open, which makes acceptance slightly looser.
pinCheck: At the pin, map_container.tsx renders <KbnDangerCallout title='Unable to initialize map' text={mapInitError}> for any init error, and mb_map.tsx _initializeMap catches and passes error.message straight to setMapInitError; no WebGL-specific handling exists. No PR in the timeline or search fixes it.

title: [Markdown] Leaving markdown edit mode was not intuitive
prompt:
[Markdown] Leaving markdown edit mode without making changes is not intuitive

Open an existing markdown panel on a dashboard for editing and make no changes. Only the "Discard" button is enabled and "Apply" is disabled. Clicking outside the panel does nothing. The user feels stuck: they did not want to click "Discard" because that implies losing changes, and the only way back to view mode is to make a change and press "Apply".

Expected: a user who opened the editor and changed nothing can leave edit mode in an obvious way that keeps what they see, for example by having "Apply" enabled, or by letting a click outside the panel return to view mode when nothing has changed.

Start in src/platform/plugins/shared/dashboard_markdown/public/components/markdown_editor.tsx. Keep the change scoped to this feature.
acceptance: With the editor open and no edits, the user has a clear way to return to view mode without pressing "Discard".
That way keeps the existing content unchanged.
When there are edits, the Apply and Discard behavior is unchanged.
whySuitable: Small UI state change; spare because the issue gives two alternative fixes, so the acceptance has to stay generic.
pinCheck: At the pin, markdown_editor.tsx computes isSaveable = Boolean(value === '' || value !== content || haveSettingsChanged) and passes it to MarkdownFooter, so Apply is disabled when nothing changed; no click-outside handler. No fixing PR found.
